correctness.rationale: The [2/2] Gauss-Padé stability function is R(z)=1−12z/(z²+6z+12). For the positive weighted star, the exact Schur resolvent with s=(3+i√3)/h yields T_0i=12|F_i|² Phi_i/(h w_i), Phi_i=A−w_i B, B>0, so the worst hub-edge is any w_i=wmax. If all Phi_i≥0, the sector bound Re(1/F_i)>0 makes each distinct leaf-leaf entry positive; spectral R(hL)>0 proves diagonals positive, and T1=1 proves stochasticity. The function Phi_star=1−Σh² w_k(wmax−w_k)/(h² w_k²+6h w_k+12) is monotone and tends to (m+1)−wmaxΣ1/w_i, giving the exact all-h criterion, one unique cutoff otherwise, and non-reentry. At h=0 T=I. Direct exact-rational computation of the full 2-stage quotient confirmed the sign criterion and row sums in 48 independently selected cases (2..5 leaves); no finite check proves arbitrary weights.
residual_risks: All-weight sufficiency depends on the complex-sector argument, not its finite tests; graph must be symmetric and strictly positive on every spoke.

originality.rationale: Generic implicit SSP restrictions, positivity-preserving graph ODE integrators, and a related pure-birth Padé positivity witness do not imply the exact sharp scalar criterion on all symmetric weighted stars; the previously described 2-leaf and unweighted-star classes are narrower. The detailed resolvent proof supplies the arbitrary-weight single-cutoff classification not located in accessible relevant primary texts. A specialized unindexed matrix-positivity result could cover it.
residual_risks: A specialized numerical analysis theorem about symmetric star Laplacians or Pade-Markov functions under equivalent conductance inequalities could be missed; search does not certify priority.

value.rationale: This determines precisely when a fourth-order A-stable completed diffusion step remains a Markov operator at every timestep on a natural heterogeneous network, and explicitly locates the first and permanent loss of positivity. The conductance ratio condition is a nonroutine exact boundary relevant to numerical positivity, not merely testing a small matrix.
residual_risks: Applies to completed step on finite symmetric positive stars, not individual implicit Gauss stages or arbitrary network topologies.

limitations: Strictly positive finite conductances; m≥2; symmetric star Laplacian; h≥0; no stagewise or nonlinear claim.
